ranked_evidence.title: Allahabad High Court Dismisses PIL Seeking Sealing of Gyanvapi Mosque Premises and Entry Ban for Non-Hindus Amid Ongoing Archaeological Survey | LawStreet
ranked_evidence.snippet: Home Judiciary Allahabad High Court Dismisses PIL Seeking Sealing of Gyanvapi Mosque Premises and Entry Ban for Non-Hindus Amid Ongoing Archaeological Survey. # Allahabad High Court Dismisses PIL Seeking Sealing of Gyanvapi Mosque Premises and Entry Ban for Non-Hindus Amid Ongoing Archaeological Survey. The Allahabad High Court has on Tuesday dismissed as withdrawn a PIL seeking the sealing of the entire Gyanvapi Mosque premises and banning entry of non-Hindus, amid the Supreme Court-approved ongoing scientific survey by Archaeological Survey of India to ascertain if the mosque has been raised over a pre-existing Hindu temple. The PIL had sought a ban on the entry of non-Hindus into the premises until the verdict in the ongoing Shringar Gauri case in which the Hindu petitioners had sought permission to worship the idols on the walls of the mosque. On August 4, the top court had rejected a plea by Anjuman Intejamia Masjid Committee Varanasi to stay the Allahabad High Court's August 3 order for the scientific survey of the premises with a direction that there would not be any excavation or use of invasive method at the site.

ranked_evidence.title: Allahabad High Court rejects PIL seeking sealing of Gyanvapi mosque premises; ASI survey to continue - The Hindu
ranked_evidence.snippet: ## District magistrate Varanasi, S Rajalingam confirmed to *The Hindu* that ASI has informed them that it will start the survey of the mosque premises (except Wazukhana) from tomorrow. The Allahabad High Court on August 3 upheld the order of Varanasi district court for conducting a ‘scientific survey’ of Gyanvyapi mosque by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). Rajalingam, confirmed to *The Hindu* that the ASI had informed the administration that it would commence the survey of the mosque premises (except the ‘wazukhana’) from Friday. While upholding the lower court’s order on the scientific survey in which the district court had asked the ASI to file a report on whether the Gyanvyapi mosque “structure” was “constructed over a pre-existing structure of a Hindu temple”, the Bench of Chief Justice Pritinker Diwaker said that once the experts in the subject matter had made it clear that the survey would not damage anything, there was no room left for doubt.
